verses.1: Yehoshaphat was seven years old when he became king.
verses.2: In the seventh year of Jehoash’s reign, he ruled for forty years. He reigned in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Zibya from Be’er Sheva.
verses.3: And Joshua did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, all the days that he served as priest.
verses.4: Only the idols remained unchanged; the people continued to worship and sacrifice to those idols.
verses.5: And Joshua said to the priests, “All the sacred money that comes into the Temple of God—that is, all the money whose value is determined by its weight—let them bring it here. All the money that can be brought into the Temple of God.”
verses.6: The priests shall take one man from among those who are sold, and they shall strengthen the doors of the house for all who may be found there.
verses.7: In the year 40 and three years after King Josiah’s reign, the priests failed to strengthen the doors of the temple.
verses.8: And King Josiah called upon Yehoyada, the priest, and the other priests. He said to them, “Do you not strengthen the doors of the temple? Now, do not take any money from your prisoners, for this money should be used to strengthen the doors of the temple.”
verses.9: And the priests were commanded not to take any money from the people, nor to strengthen the doors of the house.
verses.10: And Jehovah’s priest took one of the oxen, slaughtered it at the entrance of the Temple, and handed it over to the priests who were responsible for keeping the money that was brought into the Temple. The priests then counted all the money that was brought in.
verses.11: And it seemed that there was a great deal of money in the chest. The king’s scribe and the high priest gathered all the money that was found in the Temple of Jehovah.
verses.12: And they gave the money that was required, through the workers who were responsible for working in the house of Jehovah. They handed it over to those who cut down the trees and built the structures in the house of Jehovah.
verses.13: And for those who work in the quarries and cut down trees, and for those who gather stones from the quarries, so that they may strengthen the walls of the house of Jehovah. And for all those who go out into the mountains to do this work.
verses.14: But the Temple of Jehovah shall not be made of gold or silver objects, nor of all kinds of gold and silver items that come into the Temple of Jehovah.
verses.15: For those who work in the service of God, He will give them strength and help them to strengthen the house of Jehovah.
verses.16: And they should not consider those people who give the money to their workers as being honest people. In truth, they are indeed dishonest.
verses.17: The money of sin and the money of transgressions shall not enter the house of Jehovah among the priests.
verses.18: Then Hazael, king of Israel, will rise up and fight against Gath. He will capture it. Then Hazael will turn his face towards Jerusalem.
verses.19: And Joshua took away from the kings of Judah all the sacred objects that were sanctified by Josaphat and Jehoram. His ancestors, the kings of Judah, also took away these sacred objects along with them. He also took away all the gold that was found in the treasures of the Temple of God and in the king’s palace. Then he sent it to Joshua, the king of Aram. He went up from Jerusalem.
verses.20: And all the words of Joash, and everything he did, are recorded in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.21: And his servants stood up, tied the ropes together, and rushed down the stairs to the house of Milo.
verses.22: And Yozabad, son of Shimeath, and Yozabad, son of Shomer. His servants praised him, and he died. They buried him along with his ancestors in the city of David. Amasya, his son, became king after him.
